title: ScenarioControl: Vision-Language Controllable Vectorized Latent Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: A text prompt describing the scene and actors, or a single dashcam-style ego image; also default control tokens for agent and lane counts and a domain label.

control_mechanism.value: Cross-global control: cross-attention branch for fine-grained control plus a lightweight global-context branch; counts and domain via AdaLN-Zero; classifier-free guidance with random condition dropout.

base_model.value: Vectorized latent diffusion: transformer autoencoder over lane and object tokens plus DDPM epsilon-prediction denoiser; behaviour model for rollouts; LoRA-adapted Wan 2.2 (5B) video model for sensor video.

datasets.value: nuPlan with roughly 500K VLM-generated captions (GPT-4.1-mini on BEV renders); generalization tested on Waymo Motion.

metrics.value: Agent AP at 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 m thresholds, collision rate, control adherence (CCS, SPG, CSC at global, lane, agent levels), plus lane- and agent-level realism metrics in the appendix.

controllability_evidence.value: Image-conditioned agent-control CSC 0.2255 versus 0.0623 for Scenario Dreamer on nuPlan. Cross-global beats full cross-attention by 2.7% in agent CSC and 4.6% in AP.

stated_limitations.value: No explicit limitations section in packet. Future work: full multi-view and long-horizon visual conditioning, and unifying initial scene generation with traffic simulation to capture intent and interaction.

notes: Controls scene layout and initial agent placement more than agent behaviour; behaviour comes from a separate rollout model. The 2.7%/4.6% gain text begins mid-sentence ('over full cross-attention'), so comparison is read as against full cross-attention.
